plain_text:
Atrial fibrillation is also known as AFib or AF. AFib is the most common type of arrhythmia disorder
(when your heart beats too quickly, too slowly, or with an irregular pattern) in the world. AFib is
specifically the rapid, irregular beating of the heart's left atrium or upper chamber.
semantic_text: Atrial fibrillation is also known as AFib or AF. AFib is the most common type of arrhythmia disorder (when your heart beats too quickly, too slowly, or with an irregular pattern) in the world. AFib is specifically the rapid, irregular beating of the heart's left atrium or upper chamber.

plain_text:
According to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood
Institute, the heart's electrical system sends signals to
the different chambers of the heart. These signals make
the chambers beat regularly and ensure the heart pumps
enough blood to the rest of the body. AFib causes the
chambers to beat irregularly, which makes it harder for
the heart to pump enough blood.
semantic_text: According to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, the heart's electrical system sends signals to the different chambers of the heart. These signals make the chambers beat regularly and ensure the heart pumps enough blood to the rest of the body. AFib causes the chambers to beat irregularly, which makes it harder for the heart to pump enough blood.

plain_text:
AFib can occur in brief or infrequent episodes. It can
last for more than a week at a time, last for more than
a year, or become permanent.
semantic_text: AFib can occur in brief or infrequent episodes. It can last for more than a week at a time, last for more than a year, or become permanent.

plain_text:
Changes to the heart's tissue or electrical signaling affect
its ability to contract in rhythm. Some factors that can
cause these changes include:
semantic_text: Changes to the heart's tissue or electrical signaling affect its ability to contract in rhythm. Some factors that can cause these changes include:

plain_text:
■ High blood pressure
■ Coronary heart disease
■ Inflammation
■ Stretching, thinning, or thickening of the heart's walls
■ Fibrosis
■ Reduced blood flow to the heart
■ Buildup of proteins, cells, or minerals in the
heart tissue
semantic_text: ■ High blood pressure ■ Coronary heart disease ■ Inflammation ■ Stretching, thinning, or thickening of the heart's walls ■ Fibrosis ■ Reduced blood flow to the heart ■ Buildup of proteins, cells, or minerals in the heart tissue

plain_text:
■ Feeling tired, lightheaded, or dizzy
■ Feeling like your heart is skipping a beat, fluttering,
pounding, or beating too hard or fast
■ Chest pain
■ Low blood pressure
■ Anxiety
■ Shortness of breath
semantic_text: ■ Feeling tired, lightheaded, or dizzy ■ Feeling like your heart is skipping a beat, fluttering, pounding, or beating too hard or fast ■ Chest pain ■ Low blood pressure ■ Anxiety ■ Shortness of breath

plain_text:
It's also important to know that many people with AFib
do not experience any symptoms.
semantic_text: It's also important to know that many people with AFib do not experience any symptoms.

plain_text:
AFib can cause heart attacks and heart failure. It also
increases the risk of ischemic stroke, which occurs when a
blood clot blocks a blood vessel in the brain. This prevents
blood flow to the brain, causing brain cells to start dying.
semantic_text: AFib can cause heart attacks and heart failure. It also increases the risk of ischemic stroke, which occurs when a blood clot blocks a blood vessel in the brain. This prevents blood flow to the brain, causing brain cells to start dying.

plain_text:
In 2030, an estimated 12.1 million people
in the United States will have atrial fibrillation.
semantic_text: In 2030, an estimated 12.1 million people in the United States will have atrial fibrillation.
